## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design comprehensive data governance and privacy controls across multi-cloud and on-premises environments. It tests the candidate's capacity to translate CISSP domains into concrete, testable controls spanning data classification, access models, encryption strategies, and auditing frameworks with automation for continuous audit readiness.

## Key Concepts

- Data classification and handling frameworks
- Access control models (RBAC/ABAC) and attribute-based policy implementation
- Encryption at rest and in transit with enterprise key management (KMIP/HSM)
- Data loss prevention and comprehensive data lineage tracking
- Immutable logging and tamper-evident storage for audit trails
- Regulatory compliance and audit retention requirements
- Incident response procedures specific to data breach scenarios
- Automated testing and continuous validation for audit readiness

## Why This Is Asked

Assesses zero-trust at scale across hybrid envs with identity, posture, policy, and data governance.

## Key Concepts

- Zero Trust
- Identity-centric microsegmentation
- Short-lived tokens / OIDC
- Device posture
- SPIRE / mTLS
- CIEM & policy-as-code (OPA)
- Audit & cross-border data controls

## Code Example

```rego
package cissp.continuous_authz

default allow = false

allow {
  input.user.tenant == input.resource.tenant
  input.action in [\"read\",\"write\"]
  input.device.posture == \"compliant\"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this in a live staging environment and measure risk reductions?
- What trade-offs exist between granularity of segmentation and throughput?
